questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have previously spent time abroad in Northern and Central Europe, as well as in USA. I lacked experience from Southern Europe. I also had a personal connection to Milan. Everything considered, I had my focus on going to Milan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The education has been good, in line with what we get in Copenhagen. Most things have gone smoothly and I have gained the cultural experiences that I was looking for.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: This was not an issue at all.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did barely receive any and I didn't make use of the one that was given. This was not a major problem, however, as platforms etc work just as in Copenhagen and as I had help from friends from before, also located in Milan at the time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was some organized event but I was not available to attend at that time. Not the fault of the school in Milan. However, the program of which courses I followed had events in the beginning of the semester, as it was their first semester, but I was not receiving the info about these events and therefore missed out. I would otherwise have attended these events.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing situation in Milan is difficult to say the least. Also, the schools offer very limited housing options. You will have to accept to spend some of your extra money of Erasmus grant on housing, in order to find rooms etc in proximity to the campuses.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
That it is a rough market in Milan, numerous scammers for example.

It might be an idea to go through more established organizations, such as rent-a-home.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My only preference was to not share a room with a stranger, and if you do not accept this, there is very limited assistance from the school and you will have to look for yourself.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was not problematic.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had everything done over email before I went and didn't have issues.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus administration in Milan was very helpful with me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It works very similar to Copenhagen and I cannot think of anything specific.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The level of education was good and very similar to what we get in Copenhagen. Regarding both teachers and students. 

There is a cultural difference, however, and you will have to be open-minded regarding this. I only found this exiting, and looking away from this and considering only teaching etc, I was very satisfied.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Again, it was similar to Copenhagen. The major difference was a very theoretical approach towards teaching, a rather "classical" way of teaching. I think there are pros and cons about this approach but doing not think the difference should stop anyone from going to Milan.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As I described above.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Coding for Data Science and Data Management
Statistical and Mathematical Theory.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can only speak of the courses that I took and then I would say that both the coursesgacve a solid base in what they were aimed for. I was satisfied.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Milan is a major city and the general prize level is therefore higher than the rest of Italy/Southern Europe. Still cheaper than Copenhagen but not as cheap as I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a very nice sports club in Politecnico Citta Studi. Also a couple of events, for example a yearly trip to the alps.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: What was described above, more or less.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a lot to experience in Milan and also the proximity to both other cities and natur is great. I am thinking more in general terms here and cannot think of something specific to bring up.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other cities and the nearby nature. Boccadasse in Genova is a must. There are many trips to make and they will fill one semesters weekends, for sure

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had prior experience and knew what to expect. It is different in many ways, but also not another planet. You quickly learn some Italian behaviors and get used to them and accept them. Hopefully, you can retrieve the best parts of Italian culture and bring them back to Copenhagen, so we get a cooler coffee culture, etc :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Even in universities, the English can be a divider. However, the Italians are very open and happy to share their culture. If you are open-minded yourself, this will be no problem. Attend events, attend class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I cannot think of particular behaviors, but there are differences everywhere. This shows both in spare time but also during school work.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The classic italian stereotypical behavior. Going to the bar and ordering espresso from a grumpy Italian who does not smile. Just that it is different from home, I find fun and educating.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to take good care of the housing situation so you don't have problems with this during the semester.
Attend events etc so youre in the mix.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really. But again, try to sort the housing situation and make that work.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural experience, new friends and memories.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Mathematical Statistics was a challenge. Apart from that, some administrative stuff can be frightening in the beginning as it does not necessarily work out smoothly. Here, I advise to stay calm and not stress about having everything settled as we might be used to in Copenhagen. This is more normal state in Italy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
